[Module: torch.autograd | Symbol: Autograd_GradMode | Section: inference_mode_vs_no_grad]
torch.inference_mode vs torch.no_grad Context Managers
Both
torch.no_grad()
 and
torch.inference_mode()
 disable gradient tracking during forward evaluation.
However,
torch.inference_mode()
 is faster because it additionally disables
view tracking and version counter bumps
 on tensors.
Tensors created inside an
inference_mode
 block cannot be modified in-place outside the block or used in autograd backward passes.

tensor.detach()

).

[Module: torch.cuda | Symbol: CUDA_CachingAllocator | Section: caching_allocator_and_empty_cache]
CUDA Caching Allocator, memory_allocated vs memory_reserved, and empty_cache()
PyTorch manages GPU memory via an asynchronous caching allocator.
torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
 returns bytes occupied by active live tensors, whereas
torch.cuda.memory_reserved()
 returns total bytes held by the allocator pool (active plus cached free blocks).
torch.cuda.empty_cache()
 releases unused cached blocks back to the CUDA driver for other processes, but does not free live tensors.
Set
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
 to mitigate fragmentation OOMs.

[Module: torch.distributed | Symbol: DistributedDataParallel | Section: ddp_vs_dataparallel]
DistributedDataParallel Architecture and All-Reduce Gradient Bucketing
class torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel(module, device_ids=None, broadcast_buffers=True, find_unused_parameters=False, gradient_as_bucket_view=False, static_graph=False)
Implements multi-process data parallelism and is strongly preferred over single-process multi-threaded
torch.nn.DataParallel
 (which suffers from Python GIL contention).
DDP spawns one process per GPU via
torchrun
, initializes with
torch.distributed.init_process_group(backend='nccl')
, and overlaps backward pass computation with ring All-Reduce communication across gradient buckets (
bucket_cap_mb=25
).
Set
TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
 to abort hung NCCL collectives.

text:
[Module: torch.nn | Symbol: Conv2d | Section: shape_and_depthwise_math]
Conv2d Output Spatial Shape Formula and Depthwise Convolution
For an input tensor of shape
(N, C_in, H_in, W_in)
, the spatial output height and width of
torch.nn.Conv2d
 are computed using the floor equation:
H_out = floor((H_in + 2 * padding[0] - dilation[0] * (kernel_size[0] - 1) - 1) / stride[0] + 1)
.
When
groups == in_channels
 and
out_channels == K * in_channels
, this configuration performs a
depthwise separable convolution
 where each input channel is convolved with its own separate set of K filters.
```python
depthwise = nn.Conv2d(32, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1, groups=32)
pointwise = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=1)
```

[Module: torch.nn.utils | Symbol: clip_grad_norm_ | Section: clip_grad_norm_mechanics]
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ for Preventing Exploding Gradients
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(parameters, max_norm, norm_type=2.0, error_if_nonfinite=False)
Clips the total gradient norm of an iterable of parameters in-place to mitigate exploding gradients in RNNs, LSTMs, and Transformers.
If the total gradient norm exceeds
max_norm
, all gradients are scaled uniformly by
max_norm / (total_norm + 1e-6)
.
Call
clip_grad_norm_
 after
loss.backward()
 (and after
scaler.unscale_(optimizer)
) and before
optimizer.step()
.

[Module: torch.nn | Symbol: MultiheadAttention | Section: scaled_dot_product_overview]
torch.nn.MultiheadAttention Overview and Scaled Dot-Product Math
class torch.nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, dropout=0.0, bias=True, add_bias_kv=False, add_zero_attn=False, kdim=None, vdim=None, batch_first=False)
Computes multi-head scaled dot-product attention:
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q @ K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) @ V
.
embed_dim
 must be divisible by
num_heads
 so each head has dimension
head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
; otherwise an
AssertionError
 is raised.
Setting
batch_first=True
 changes tensor layout from
(seq_len, batch, embed_dim)
 to
(batch, seq_len, embed_dim)
.

 of shape

class torch.nn.BatchNorm2d(num_features, eps=1e-05, momentum=0.1, affine=True, track_running_stats=True)
Normalizes 4D inputs
(N, C, H, W)
 per channel across batch and spatial dimensions with default stability constant
eps=1e-05
.
During
model.train()
, buffers
running_mean
 and
running_var
 update via exponential moving average with
momentum=0.1
:
running_stat_new = (1 - momentum) * running_stat_old + momentum * batch_stat_observed
.
During
model.eval()
, running statistics are frozen.

[Module: torch.nn | Symbol: BatchNorm2d_LayerNorm | Section: layernorm_vs_batchnorm]
torch.nn.LayerNorm Per-Sample Normalization for Transformers
class torch.nn.LayerNorm(normalized_shape, eps=1e-05, elementwise_affine=True, bias=True)
Unlike BatchNorm,
LayerNorm
 computes mean and variance independently per sample across the last D dimensions given by
normalized_shape
.
It maintains no running statistics, behaves identically in
train()
 and
eval()
 modes, and is invariant to batch size for Transformer sequences.

torch.nn.LSTM Gate Equations and Hidden States
class torch.nn.LSTM(input_size, hidden_size, num_layers=1, bias=True, batch_first=False, dropout=0.0, bidirectional=False)
Applies a multi-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network.
At each timestep t, the cell maintains hidden state
h_t
 and cell state
c_t
 regulated by input gate
i_t
, forget gate
f_t
, cell candidate
g_t
, and output gate
o_t
.
When
bidirectional=True
, output hidden dimension doubles to
2 * hidden_size
.
Note:
dropout
 applies between stacked layers except the last layer, so setting
dropout > 0
 with
num_layers=1
 triggers a UserWarning and has no effect.

[Module: torch.nn | Symbol: LSTM | Section: pack_padded_sequence_handling]
Handling Variable-Length Sequences with pack_padded_sequence
To prevent recurrent layers like
nn.LSTM
 from wasting computation over trailing padding tokens, wrap padded batches using
torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(input, lengths, batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)
 before the LSTM, and unpack outputs back to padded tensors using
torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence
.

[Module: torch.optim | Symbol: AdamW | Section: decoupled_weight_decay_math]
torch.optim.AdamW Decoupled Weight Decay vs L2 Regularization
class torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=0.001, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-08, weight_decay=0.01, amsgrad=False, fused=None)
Implements AdamW decoupled weight decay regularization.
Unlike standard
torch.optim.Adam
 where L2 penalty is added to the gradient before computing adaptive moments
m_t
 and
v_t
,
AdamW
 subtracts
lr * weight_decay * theta_t
 directly from weights simultaneously with the moment step.
Setting
fused=True
 on CUDA launches a single fused multi-tensor kernel update.

text:
[Module: torch.optim | Symbol: AdamW | Section: parameter_groups_no_decay]
Excluding Bias and LayerNorm Parameters from Weight Decay
When training Transformers with
AdamW
, 1D parameters such as bias vectors and
LayerNorm
 /
BatchNorm
 affine scale weights should be excluded from weight decay (
weight_decay=0.0
) using optimizer parameter group dicts.
```python
optim_groups = [
    {'params': [p for p in model.parameters() if p.dim() >= 2], 'weight_decay': 0.01},
    {'params': [p for p in model.parameters() if p.dim() < 2], 'weight_decay': 0.0},
]
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(optim_groups, lr=3e-4, fused=True)
```

[Module: torch.optim.lr_scheduler | Symbol: OneCycleLR_CosineAnnealingLR | Section: onecyclelr_super_convergence]
torch.optim.lr_scheduler.OneCycleLR Super-Convergence Schedule
class torch.optim.lr_scheduler.OneCycleLR(optimizer, max_lr, total_steps=None, pct_start=0.3, anneal_strategy='cos', div_factor=25.0, final_div_factor=10000.0)
Warms up the learning rate from
initial_lr = max_lr / div_factor
 to
max_lr
 over the first
pct_start
 (default 0.3) fraction of total steps, then anneals down to
initial_lr / final_div_factor
.
Unlike epoch-level schedulers,
OneCycleLR.step()
 must be called after every single training batch iteration.

[Module: torch.ao.quantization | Symbol: Quantization_PTQ_QAT | Section: dynamic_vs_static_ptq_qat]
Dynamic Quantization vs Static Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) vs QAT
PyTorch offers three INT8 quantization modes: (1)
Dynamic Quantization
 (
quantize_dynamic
) quantizes weights to
torch.qint8
 ahead of time while computing activation scales dynamically at runtime (ideal for LSTMs and Linear layers); (2)
Static PTQ
 calibrates activation observers on representative data before
convert_fx
; (3)
Quantization-Aware Training (QAT)
 inserts
FakeQuantize
 modules during training with straight-through estimators (STE).

[Module: torch | Symbol: save_load_state_dict | Section: weights_only_security_and_map_location]
Secure Checkpoint Loading with weights_only=True and map_location
torch.load(f, map_location=None, *, weights_only=True, mmap=None)
Passing
weights_only=True
 prevents arbitrary pickle code execution by restricting deserialization to tensors and primitive dicts.
Use
map_location=torch.device('cpu')
 when loading GPU checkpoints onto CPU or remapping across distributed ranks, and
mmap=True
 to memory-map large checkpoint files without spiking host RAM.

text:
[Module: torch | Symbol: Tensor_Views_Contiguity | Section: view_vs_reshape_contiguous]
Memory Strides, Contiguity, and tensor.view() vs tensor.reshape()
Operations like
transpose()
 and
permute()
 return a view sharing storage with modified strides, making the tensor non-contiguous (
tensor.is_contiguous() == False
).
Calling
tensor.view(*shape)
 on a non-contiguous tensor raises a
RuntimeError
 unless
tensor.contiguous().view(*shape)
 is called first.
tensor.reshape(*shape)
 returns a view when contiguous and copies data automatically when non-contiguous.

text:
[Module: torch.utils.data | Symbol: DataLoader | Section: multiprocess_workers_and_memory]
DataLoader Multiprocessing, pin_memory, and persistent_workers
class torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=1, shuffle=False, sampler=None, num_workers=0, collate_fn=None, pin_memory=False, drop_last=False, prefetch_factor=None, persistent_workers=False)
Setting
pin_memory=True
 allocates fetched host tensors in page-locked (pinned) RAM for fast asynchronous DMA transfers to CUDA GPUs via
tensor.to(device, non_blocking=True)
.
Setting
persistent_workers=True
 keeps worker subprocesses alive across epochs instead of shutting down and respawning workers after every epoch.
Default
prefetch_factor
 is 2 when
num_workers > 0
.

[Module: torch.utils.data | Symbol: DataLoader | Section: custom_collate_fn_and_samplers]
Custom collate_fn and DistributedSampler Usage
The
collate_fn
 callable merges a list of dataset samples into a mini-batch and handles variable-length sequence padding.
In multi-GPU training with
DistributedSampler
, set
shuffle=False
 on the DataLoader and call
sampler.set_epoch(epoch)
 at the start of every epoch to guarantee deterministic random shuffling across epochs.
